answer: We formulate dynamic opportunity-cost bonds paired with a subgame-perfect slashing matrix, forcing adversaries who forge identity splits to lock capital calibrated to each epoch pulse. Capital barrier analysis proves expected Sybil payoffs fall strictly below zero past a convex risk ridge, as identity multiplication costs scale superlinearly against linear payouts. This yields convergence to a strict Nash equilibrium where single-identity honest validation dominates adversarial fragmentation.
